- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.30) — model fails to capture downward momentum, often lagging by 1–3 days.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — model reacts too quickly to sentiment changes, leading to overshoots or undershoots.
- Mean-reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves or too low after sharp drops — adjust by smoothing recent extremes.
- For 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast magnitude if sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish (sentiment < 0.05) — model tends to overcompensate.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for persistent downside risk.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals without confirming sentiment reversal — model often predicts continuation after sentiment shifts.
